Why I hate the finals and Embark: An autobiography

My name is MrEden111, often known as Eden, especially in circles on the finals as one of the most dedicated exclusive charge’n’slam sledge players since season 4 from Oceania. 

The finals is, and more importantly, *was* a wonderful game, a breath of fresh air in a stale live service industry where your wallet was valued, you as a player was respected, and where the developers would constantly deliver breath taking updates. But having not played season 3, I had little idea of the horrors there were yet to come.

For many seasons the game was pumped with life, after the tremendous success of season 4 with a vast array of new content such as sponsorships, new weapons, and my all-time favourite map; fortune stadium. They would swing hard again with season 5, with Mexico themed beauty bringing in even more content (despite how op the Cerberus was), season 6 bringing even more wonder ignoring the Vegas reskin which was much better than its original predecessor (No the team death match map does not count) … but then came season 7. Because even accounting for the flaws, these were updates that did amazing for the health of the game. Alongside also dealing with issues such as the infamous taser (which later turned to the disabler) to rise player enjoyment.

But I wake up in the morning of season 7, and I open to read the patch notes, my hands went cold and palmy, my heart sank to rest on my lungs. The infamous sledge nerf, the turning point of the game for me and finally opened my eyes to the faults of Embark. Which as a noteworthy mention, was only caused because of this obsession in the heavy playerbase to use winch with the most current powerful weapon, leading to only the weapon being significantly nerfed, which is a relevant issue in the mindset of embark’s balancing philosophy to always look at the surface of the issue instead of the deeper reasons (unless if they outright ignore it of course).

It was then Embark took a turn for me, it was the first season they introduced the $50 ultimate battle trash and pushing out more and more expensive reskins/clothing, prioritising the store (which became even more evident in the future). They started to become more ignorant to the real issues plaguing the game in favour of streamers, they reduced the servers to cut costs down which made international play even worse and even made playing in your own country laggy just to min max profit margins. Melee as a whole by that point had been entirely side lined and made useless while lights became more of a major issue for the casual player base, with most solutions to the issue only worsening overall player enjoyment such as with the cl04 especially. 

This all became worse by season 8, the infamous Esports season, for 110 days the game did not receive a single major balance nor particularly small one either because embark refused to endanger their forced esports. They lied to us and themselves that it would bring in new players when in fact it was the most damaging time for the playerbase since season 3.  But embark will never have the humility to admit that they failed the players, because they are always right in their eyes with every decision they make and still intend to make season 12 a repeat having learned none of these mistakes.

Things got worse when Arc Raiders released, with an even smaller team, Embark rather than risking their profits. Focused their efforts on making store items before anything else as before every store update had an array of balance changes but it soon became just small footnotes. Leading to significantly less content overall and started to pour out half baked ideas such as the P90 (a glorified light smg for medium), the crossbow which is a reskinned pike, the sad joke of a hover pad and much else, which did little to improve the staling variety for the long-time players like me who made the majority of the player base (and their revenue). This also led to terrible balancing choices that left light just too powerful in the casual scene and left medium as well as heavy weaker, with guns like the light's m11 able to spray down a heavy in seconds with just hip fire.

But the melee was worst of all, melee has been the beaten children of the finals where especially heavy and medium have suffered the worse. Spear didn’t get a major update since season 3 and even took away the ability to emote cancel heavy attack somewhere around season 7 and then proceeded to NERF IT in the melee rework despite being the least popular melee weapon alongside taking away the popular fling technique. Riot shield got its ability to run at angles taken away because screw them I guess no unintended tech allowed for melee. But as a pure example of how Embark does not playtest their ideas at all prior to the new season, riot shield has become THE melee weapon with its shove and great damage making it way too powerful which I’m sure embark will swiftly nerf sooner or later.

With Sledge on the other end of the spectrum where it used the be the symbol of final melee down reduced to its kneecaps broken and now is just a mindless spam weapon where I long for the days you could do combos pre nerf with quick melee (rip m1 + qm = dead light). With the only other strong melee now just being the sword which despite what Embark has said, has only buffed its spamability by making m1 be almost as strong as lunge. The melee rework especially has done nothing to solve the issues of melee being unviable and still leaving melee as a braindead spam weapon category rather than anything that could be take seriously than just a pathetic annoying joke that ticks everyone off, me a sledge player included.

If you have read this far, I applaud you, I could go on all day, but I digress. Do not waste your time on this game, please. While it may be fun for a time, but in the end, it leaves you dead and hollow, wishing it felt as wonderful when you first played. Any hope I had in these Developers to make my favourite game great again have long since passed, and this mockery of a melee rework has put out the candle of whatever passion I had left.

Sincerely, Eden

THE FINALS is hands down my absolute favorite shooter right now. The fast-paced rhythm, the chaotic environmental destruction, and the cosmetic options are entirely incredible. My favorite class to play is the Light, and I absolutely love running the M11, the sword, and the FCAR. My absolute favorite game modes are Power Shift and Quick Cash.

Performance-running on a High-End PC is great. I play at maximum graphical settings without DLSS and manage to get around 90 FPS. This is perfectly acceptable since the game is visually heavy and packed with physics. Speaking of atmosphere, the soundtrack is unique. I highly recommend activating the music mix option from previous seasons because every single track is incredible. 

I started playing back in Season 10, and now that we are in Season 11, the progression system feels amazing. The ability to unlock past seasonal skins using Multibucks makes it feel like you have two or three battle passes active at the same time. The Year 1 bundle is a fantastic deal that unlocks a massive part of previous seasons. For Season 11, I got the Ultimate Pass with legendary skins, which looks brutal and helps support the developers. The weapon charms, weapon skins, character outfits, emotes, stickers, and badges are top-tier. My only personal wish would be for more flawless female character faces and pink skins. 

The battle pass is highly rewarding, and the cosmetic bundles are very reasonably priced. The game is obviously at its absolute best when playing with friends, and I rarely encounter cheaters. The only downside preventing a perfect score is the matchmaking system, which can feel quite unbalanced when putting level 1 players against level 100 players in the same lobby. There should also be heavier penalties for players who leave matches before they end. Despite these minor issues, the game is dangerously addictive. Highly recommended. Final score: 9.5/10.

The Finals is one of the best games out there that perfectly captures the arena shooter genre with its own unique style. Despite putting 1,000 hours into it, my biggest grievance is the constant, relentless updates and rebalances. Buffing, nerfing, and reworking weapons and abilities every 1 to 2 months drastically kills the game's flow and overall enjoyment.

It takes about 50 hours on average to truly master and get used to a weapon, but thanks to the developers at Embark, they tweak the weapon stats right around that time, completely ruining your playstyle. The worst part is that this is a never-ending cycle. I won't even get into the increasing number of bugs and the performance/FPS drops with every single patch.

I am calling out to the developers: stop messing with the game balance, or at least find a healthy middle ground. It feels as though these adjustments are being made by people who don't even play the game. For example—how on earth can the FAMAS be weaker and have a smaller magazine capacity than the FCAR? There are countless examples like this, but I won’t waste my breath. Just leave the game alone.

Finally, a game that encourages anything and everything to secure your advantage with little to no limits on how you design your loadout and abilities, no predetermined "hero" characters but rather extreme customization of your contestant, and no control of the arena and its unpredictable destruction.

I've played a lot of FPS games over the years, and honestly, The Finals is one of the most innovative and fun ones on the market right now. The fact that it's completely free makes it even better.

There's a huge variety of weapons, and with three different classes to choose from, every match feels different. You constantly run into new strategies, team comps, and crazy moments, so the gameplay rarely gets stale. The destructible environments add another layer of chaos that keeps every fight exciting.

The cosmetics are also some of the best I've seen in any game. They're creative, high quality, and let you make your character look unique without everything feeling like a copy-and-paste skin.

If you're looking for a fast-paced FPS that actually feels fresh instead of copying every other shooter out there, give The Finals a shot. It's free, it's fun, and it's one of the few games that keeps me coming back for "just one more match."

Personal Experience:
As someone who enjoys fast-paced multiplayer shooters, The Finals quickly became one of my favorite games. From my very first match, I realized that it offers something different from most FPS games. The fully destructible environments make every match feel unique, and I never know exactly what will happen next. Instead of relying only on aiming skills, the game rewards creativity, teamwork, and quick decision-making. Every victory feels satisfying because it usually comes from smart strategies rather than just getting the most eliminations.
Positive Aspects:
The biggest strength of The Finals is its destructible environment. Being able to destroy walls, floors, and entire buildings completely changes how matches are played. Teamwork is another major highlight, as communication and coordination often determine the winner. The game also features smooth movement, exciting gunplay, and a good variety of weapons, gadgets, and character classes. Its graphics, sound effects, and game show presentation create an exciting atmosphere that makes every match feel intense and entertaining. Frequent seasonal updates also keep the game fresh with new content.
Negative Aspects:
Despite its strengths, The Finals still has some weaknesses. Weapon and gadget balance can sometimes become an issue after updates, making certain loadouts much stronger than others. Matchmaking is not always consistent, occasionally placing highly skilled players against beginners, which can lead to frustrating matches. Playing with uncooperative teammates can also make the experience much less enjoyable. In addition, server issues or minor bugs sometimes affect gameplay, especially during busy periods.
Suggestions for Improvement:
I believe the developers can make The Finals even better by continuing to improve weapon and class balance with regular updates. Matchmaking should be more accurate to create fairer matches for players of all skill levels. Adding more maps, game modes, and seasonal events would help keep the game exciting over the long term. Stronger anti-cheat measures and better server stability would also improve the overall experience. Finally, introducing more creative rewards and progression systems would encourage players to stay active and continue improving.
Conclusion:
Overall, I think The Finals is one of the most creative multiplayer shooters released in recent years. Its combination of destruction, teamwork, and fast-paced gameplay makes it stand out from other FPS games. Although it still has areas that need improvement, the positive aspects far outweigh the negatives. I genuinely enjoy playing it and believe that with continued support and updates from the developers, The Finals has the potential to remain one of the best competitive online shooters for many years.

The Finals is easily one of the most underrated shooters I’ve played. I liked all the game modes, but spent most of my time in World Tour grinding the Deep Pockets achievement.

Gunplay is really good and I’d describe it as a polished Apex Legends. Movement is great too and fits the fast pace perfectly.

Destruction is probably my favorite part of the game. You can destroy enemy positions, make your own paths or even use it to move around the map faster. It looks great and actually affects how you play instead of just being there for show.

The classes are well balanced, especially when you’re playing with a team and everyone runs a different build properly. The maps are also amazing. Bernal, Seoul and Monaco were my favorites, but honestly all of them are great.

Progression is pretty fast, unless you start caring about achievements haha. Weapons could use a bit more variety, but it’s nothing that hurts the experience. Players are pretty random and the skill gap is definitely noticeable.

Graphics are great, performance was perfect for me and monetization is completely optional without constantly being shoved in your face.

The best part is easily the fast-paced gameplay and the freedom you have. The worst part is the achievement grind. Period.

Definitely recommend it. It’s not doing anything completely new, but it does what it does really well and deserves way more attention.

The map is almost 100% destructible, and none of that destruction is scripted. The skins system is unique and customizable while still cohesive, and the weapon skins have effort put into them. A skin that might at first seem like just a recolor, you might notice a slight tweak in the suppressor model, or a different grip texture, small things that show the devs care. The gun handling and sound design are both fantastic, and the visuals are vibrant and beautiful. 

This is what Unreal Engine 5 games should be.

THE FINALS — 3/10
Credit where it's due: the graphics look clean, the soundtrack is fire, and the destruction physics are impressive. But the community and sweat culture absolutely ruin this game.
Low-tier Bronze and Silver lobbies are playable, but as soon as you hit mid-to-high Gold, it completely falls apart for casuals. It’s an absolute magnet for ex-Fortnite sweats who treat grinding cash outs like a full-time 9-to-5 job and refuse to touch grass.
The community will beg and plead with you to play, but they conveniently leave out the fact that trying to rank up is the literal video game definition of the Sisyphus meme—pushing the boulder all the way up just to watch it roll right back down. Solid engine and great physics, completely ruined by the player base.

More people would play this awesome game if it wasn't for the fact that Embark doesn't know how to run or maintain games. However, they do know how to make great games, and this is definitely a great game. 100% would recommend.

This is why this game is not more popular than it is as a competitive game. Stick to casual if you're gonna play.

The Finals is one of the most fun multiplayer games I have ever played, and it deserves far more love than it gets. The destruction is incredible. Buildings can collapse around you, walls can be blown open to create new paths, and an entire match can change because someone destroyed the floor beneath the objective. That chaos makes every round feel unpredictable instead of playing out the same way every time.

The movement and gunplay both feel great. The different classes, weapons, gadgets, and builds give the game so much variety. You can support your team, defend an objective, destroy half the arena, or pull off something completely ridiculous that somehow wins the match. Teamwork matters, but the game still gives every player plenty of ways to make a big play.

The game-show presentation ties everything together. The announcers, music (the soundtrack is top 10), sound effects (Embark SFX is top 3), crowds, arenas, and overall style give The Finals an identity that most modern shooters do not have. It is exciting, chaotic, creative, and simply a great time. Everyone should at least try it.

Let me just say it: this game is super fun.

The skins are insane — genuinely some of the most creative and well-made cosmetics I've seen in a multiplayer shooter. The audio design is excellent, giving every explosion, footstep, and cashout buzzer a satisfying punch. The way people turn into coins when they die hits and itch I didn't know I had. And the destruction? Best in the business, no contest. Walls crumble, floors collapse, and entire buildings come down around you in a way no other game has pulled off this well. And it changes the environment. It doesn't just delete a wall from the map. It moves it and by the end of the match it's like a jungle gym. 

Now, the big caveat: the onboarding is rough. If you're not a 16-year-old who just downed four cans of energy drinks before slamming the queue button, you will struggle early on. The learning curve hits hard, and the game doesn't exactly hold your hand. You'll die a lot. You'll wonder what just killed you. You'll question your life choices.
But if you're patient and don't mind eating some dirt in the beginning, it clicks — and when it does, it's incredibly rewarding. I'm just a guy in his 20s trying to keep up, and I'm having a ton of fun with it.

TL;DR: Give it a shot. It's free, there's zero pay-to-win, and once you push through the initial chaos, you'll find one of the most entertaining shooters out there right now.

The devs claim to fix things each new season, but somehow nothing ever changes. The meta stays exactly the same, and you keep dying to the same classes and loadouts match after match. After my last game, I found myself thinking: "Am I playing this wrong? Am I supposed to pick the easiest weapons rather than the ones I actually want to use?" Maybe. But even if that's by design, why would the devs invalidate over half the weapons in the game by making them uncompetitive? Back when I played Counter-Strike: Source, the only guns anyone ever used were the M4, the AK, the AWP, and the Deagle. Is that really better than Counter-Strike 2, where far more weapons have utility and you can choose what suits your playstyle?

The Light class is arguably the most infuriating to counter as any other class. Evasive Dash turns several of the Light's weapons into a dominant meta. Throwing knives, the sword, and the double-barrel shotgun all seem to have a lower TTK than any other ranged weapon in the game.

Honestly, Titanfall 2 had a host of interesting weapons with fun properties and unique traits, and—with maybe a few exceptions - I never got tilted when I died in that game. When I get killed by a Kraber shot from a grapple-hooking speedster on the other side of the map, I know that person didn't just get lucky; they probably practiced a lot to pull that off. Meanwhile, none of the weapons in The Finals reward me for dedicating time to them, nor do they feel satisfying when I'm on the receiving end.

I want to echo what others have said about the movement, creativity, destruction, and gunplay (all excellent!), but I also wanted to sing some praises to other aspects of the game that are fantastic but often overlooked: The music and sound design are both absolutely phenomenal, the game is optimized very well (runs great on the Steam Deck!), the gameshow ambience is so creative and immersive, and having a multiplayer FPS with crossplay, no lootboxes, and anti-cheat compatible with Linux is such a breath of fresh air (I'm looking at you Bungie 😡). The cosmetics are also better than any other game I've seen, hands down. You want to play with your weapons as cardboard? You want a mini roller-coaster wrapped around your gun with moving carts and lights? You want to throw a grenade disguised as a stuffed animal? You want to run around with a giant spoon smashing people? Or do you want to go all serious and dress-up in full realistic military apparel? All check.

Players like to complain about balance, but honestly the weapons and gadgets are all also balanced very well. Besides perhaps the pinnacle of pro play, every weapon and gadget is viable in competitive play, and the devs do a good job at shifting the meta with updates without destroying playstyles. I don't know how they manage to balance a game that well in a game that is so dynamic and unpredictable, but I think they've done a fantastic job.

I do have some complaints about the game that I think are important to mention, and hopefully the devs can address these. Servers can be pretty unstable at times, even with good internet. Getting disconnected or connected late, or having teammates with those same issues is unfortunately fairly common. Matchmaking in ranked mode can also be pretty unfair at times, and you can lose rank points from situations outside your control. The player-base can also be pretty toxic at times, and you'll definitely be blamed for something at some point by your teammates :)
But all of these issues are really issues from multiplayer games in general, not so much specific to the Finals.

Overall I would highly recommend The Finals, and am surprised that it is not more popular than it is.

My reasons for not recommending this game isn't because of the game itself, but from the poorly though out controller implementation as someone who primarily uses gyro aiming when I'm playing shooters on a controller. If you're a keyboard and mouse player, or someone who uses standard controls, this complaint may not apply. 

My major complaint is the lack of support for gyro aiming on any controller other than a DualShock/DualSense plugged in via USB. On top of this, there is a lack of support for proper mixed input, which is where both mouse and controller inputs can be used at the same time without stutters from it locking the inputs of one or the other or GUI glyph flickering, forcing me to bind everything to KBM inputs and losing benefits that other controller owners with gyro sensors don't have to deal with. While I can just bind everything to KBM inputs through Steam Input and have these issues resolved, there have been reports of bans for using virtual input devices which is how Steam Input works so it's too risky for me to continue playing like this. This even extends to other programs like DS4Windows which uses a virtual DS4 controller and is useful to get gyro support for Dualshock 4 controllers connected via bluetooth. This could be fixed by supporting native gyro for the Steam Controller and Steam Deck if there is a concern of cheating software being spoofed as Steam Input virtual devices, but for now nothing has been done about this. Risking bans for using Steam Input like I'm playing Valorant is deeply frustrating.

Loading screen animation ? Nobody look that and it is leggit 2-3 seconds of watching anyway, your contestant is always up front so are other people really looking at you ? I dont think so.  
Animation in game ? Stickers ? Grafiti ? Emotes ? Who use that ? I never seen anyone using them in 44 hours of gameplay. Why should I waste precious money on these ?

2700 credits for a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ skin ? What is this ?

This is a nightmare.

If you finish the battlepass, you'll earn just enough to buy another battle pass (1570 credit I think). But then you wont be able to buy skins unless you pay with real money for them. So you want to use your battle pass credit for the next season or for skins ? Make your choice (and 1570 credits wont give you much choice of skins pack). 

The amount of microtransaction in this game is insane. And the price of stuff in way more insane. 
I know it is a free to play, you can 100% play this game without paying any dollars. 
But you will quickly find it boring and unattractive. There's nothing to unlock or to do if you are not paying for anything. After just some days of gameplay you will have discover and tried every gameplay. 

This new tendancy in the gaming community must stop. I would prefer to pay 20-50$ for a game like this and have more free stuff in the game to unlock than having to play it for free but pay to unlock everything. I mean each battle pass mean you will after multiple year have paid more than 100-200$ for this game. Is it serious ? 

Just remember this : this system is there because it work. It make profits for corporation. It is a spreading cancer and it must stop. This system use our psyche and is pretty damn close as dependance created by lotery games, gambling and psychoactive substances. We want more dopamine rush by buying one more skin. Because the game itself doesnt offer you enough dopamine. But some days after that the skin is already boring and the dopamine stopped so we must buy another one to get dopamine again. Why would I be the only looser without any skin anyway ? The peer pressure is working hard. 

Ok so now about the game itself : 

1) The tutorial suck. 
2) The matchmaking is absolutly horrible. As a newcomer YOU WILL play mostly against insane try hard and sweaty kids. YOU WILL play against a lot of them and they will break you. The problem is not them. Their skills are insane. I'm not one of those who accuse everyone of cheating. The problem is that in a competitive game with no servers browsers, the matchmaking system put you in a same lobby as high levels players. This is as trash for you that it is for them. No one is getting better at the game by being opposed to the other extreme. It is just so frustrating. At the moment I'm about 30-40 wins and maybe 700-1200 eliminations. But I'm always against hundreds of wins and multiples thousands of eliminations. How am I supposed to compete and have fun against that ? Also, while solo queued, I know I'll be fighting against premade full of friends. This is a major problem. 
3) This is a classic but for a team based game, people doesnt know or doesnt want to team-play and collaborate. YOU WILL play will people that go attacking alone a full enemy crew. You will have friend who dont revive anyone of your team. You'll be on your own.  
4) This point follow the one above, but people will almost never communicate with you. They do not use their microphone, they do not use the ping system and they do not use the chat (except for insulting each other as any toxic community in these type of game do). I have my microphone on, I salute people on entering the lobby, I try to communicate, but no one respond. 
5) The melee is so out of place, this game is already so chaotic, in my opinion the melee system is way too much. I get one shot so many time by light build with swords, this is absurd. I know this point will be controversial because a lot of people say now it was nerfed the melee suck but honestly while I am bad at it there is people out there that are absolutly amazing with melee weapon and to me in a gun fight it make no sens. 
6) I dislike people saying those kind of thing, but I think the game is indeed dying. When the game came out it reached about 200 000 and more players. But only after 2 months it fell to less than 50 000 players. Now the players amount is between 14 000 and 19 000 players. When a new season come out the playerbase kinda raise up a little but honestly the game had its time and I'm trying it too late sadly. After all, its a 3 years old game that didnt evolve that much and doesnt offer a lot either. 
7) The servers sucks. I lag so much and have stutters, this is the only game where I have that, I have a really good internet connexion. 
8) A lot of time I get killed fleeing a battle and die when I reach a cover and I'm behind it. A lot of people say to me this have to do with the servers. While in your screen you are behind cover, the other player still saw you uncovered in his screen. So most of the time fleeing isnt good : you will die even if you have reach a secure position. 

Is this all bad ? 
Why am I still playing after 44 hours ? 
Well, the game look pretty good visually. It's nice after the mobile-looking visual of Fornite, Apex, Overwatch and others of these type of game. 
The gunplay is pretty fun too, I mean it's fluid and make me think of a mix between Titanfall and Apex. 
The game mode is interesting, kinda like a search and destroy type of game. It's refreshing and fun. 
The character creation is fun, I mean if you put aside the fact that is cost so much. 

If you're sure you gonna play with a lot of friends and never solo queued, I would say go for it, try it. It's free to play. Just dont do the same error as me : wait about a month before buying the battle pass. 

And damn, I bought the battle pass for almost 50 CAD $. I must play to make use of those precious pennies I spent on this game :') 
I'll probably stop when the season end or before it.

I really wanna give this game a thumbs up, I really do.
Conceptually, The Finals is a very unique sandbox FPS where the environment is at your disposal. Every building and object in the game can be interacted with, or destroyed. The chaotic destruction keeps every match feeling different and fresh. There are 3 different classes; Small, Medium, and Heavy; Each one has its own unique guns, equipment, and abilities, there's a build suitable for everyone. The game is truly 1 of 1 in this regard, it really is an interesting spin on the classic FPS genre.
Unfortunately, that's where my praise for The Finals ends. I've never played a game with such an out of touch development team, every patch note I read ends with an exaggerated sigh. Each new season has pulled the game further and further away from the potential it once had. If I had a nickel for every time me or a friend has complained about an update, I could probably afford this game's 30 DOLLAR BATTLE PASS LMAOOO. 
That's another complaint I have, The Microtransactions. I get it, The Finals is free and they gotta make money somehow, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this is not the way. Every time I launch the game, I'm immediately hit with a cutscene shoving the new outfits down my throat. Not once, Every. Single. Time. The In-Game Shop is just as laughable as those cutscenes; Every Battle Pass, Old or New, can be purchased, ruining the whole point of collecting limited time items each season. 
I hope that one day I can come back and change my review, because The Finals is a really fun game, but Embark Studios has left it in a state that I simply cant recommend.

Before the melee rework, the existing system felt frustrating, and a bit unfair. Now, after the rework, it feels EXTREMELY frustrating, very unfair, and every melee weapon has its own confusing rules.
I started by ignoring those weapons, and the opponents that used them would feel irritating.
I then try to use them because "if something is meta use it", but they're not even strong. Now they all have an even more simplified gameplan and no real skill expression, while also not being balanced.
 
- Spear is straight up worse compared to before the update, where all combos deal less damage and heavy hits are harder to land since if you miss one you can't use them for a while. A weapon that already was considered the worst by a lot of the community is now completely, entirely unusable. 
- Sledge feels unbeatable with any class unless the user pushes you in full open from 50 meters away or more letting you shoot them, on a class that can close distances very easily. In a vacuum, the 1v1 is somewhat balanced, sure. But in a real game it feels like it's a 70/30 for the hammer user, where if he manages to get close he has already won with no player interaction being really relevant.
- Twin blades were frustrating and boring before, so you change nothing about them except granting them more range, so they now also feel inescapable.
- Riot used to be inconsistent with blocking, now it's even worse where I'll be looking at someone and they still hit me while aiming at the body. You try to block and quickly hit, and you get punished by the new "special attack" that takes away your defense and locks you in an animation for half an hour.
- Everything else hasn't even changed much and feels just as frustrating and boring.

This whole rework is just very, very unfun. It's genuinely just worse than before, and the worst part has to be the 25 damage quick melee. It was perfectly balanced and fun before, not one person on earth said 40 damage was too much for quick melee, and it was a useful option when you ran out of bullets. Now that it does 25 it's genuinely unusable. Worse than a last resort, since reloading and shooting again genuinely has higher DPS than melee-ing until you kill the opponent. No point in pressing the melee button, the only good part about the rework is the quick melee knockback but even that doesn't proc half the time. 

This rework has hurt the game more than anything else up to now and rolling it back would only make the game more fun again for everyone, except sledge users I guess, lol. Casual gameplay has never been this unfun, even open beta with its bad performance and crashes felt better. Though it's nice to know the devs put more time in not listening to the userbase with these updates instead of fixing thermal vision. We are never seeing THAT gadget again.

Its so very sad. ive dumped hundreds of hours into this game between steam and xbox. I work and am miserable and used to get so exited to come home to be able to relax and play my favorite game. Now it just throws me into a fit of rage. I really wanted to love this game but if your competitive like me or strive to become higher in rank or get better at the game well your SOL. The solo queing is miserable and even if you do have a team 90% of the ranked games or hell even casual youll run in to 
1.) people using unbalanced guns (or melee weapons)
2.) an atrocious rank score calculation system
3.) people playing on smurf accounts
4.) people using cheats to virtually make recoil dissapear
5.) Teams consistently finding any way except the intended way to play the game
As mentioned previously i am competitive yes but i have never been this aggravated by a game. When playing the ranked system the score you gain or lose is calibrated based on what seed your team is determined as. this has various issues such as its very reward limiting when you win and very punishing when you lose. You could gain 1000+ rank score from placing first, however you can loose 900+ for getting knocked out in the first round depending on your seeding and i know what your thinking; well surely youll place first more often after playing the game more, learning the mechanics, bettering your skill. and you couldnt be further from wrong. The massive amounts of variables like the lack of consistent teammates, the rank score gain or loss changes every single game, or when a teammates leaves at the beginning of a match will just put you in a chokehold for an unattainable goal many of us will not be able to achieve. Another perfect example of why this game is only going to make you miserable, this just happened to me right before writing this. I had solo qued into a ranked game; we had 1st seed meaning if we finished the bracket in first we would gain 900 rank score, however if we did not at least place 3rd we would lose rank score. 7/8th place would result in a loss of approx 800. Already does not seem like a fair trade off right? i mean statistically your going to place first only a handful of times in a 8 hour session or longer. Well youll run into more issues when your teammate disconnects at the very beginning of the match. and yes i understand this is not the developer or games fault but only being in teams of 3 each member of the team is extremely important. losing one for the entire match is almost always a gaurenteed loss. as i mentioned previously this is not the game or developers fault and they cannot control the actions of their players however they provide a compensation in points when your teammate abandons the match. this compensation is typically around 200 rank score. Just think about that. you are 98% of the time gaurenteed a loss when your 1 teammate down yet your still losing 600-700 rank score even with compensation. one game like that, that may not even be in your control mind you will totally erase hours of work if you consistently place 3rd and 4th only gaining an average of 200-300 rank score per third place and 40-60 ranked score per 4th place. as i mentioned previously its an unattaniable goal to aim for higher ranks and its extremely annoying to spend so many hours and end up right back where you started a week ago due to poor games or bad teammates. Say what you will thats its a skill issue on my part or its just a video game so this stuff shouldnt matter that much but when your a dad or mom working a full time job and all you do is crave relief from the real world. so you hop on your favorite game to decompress and end up feeling so so much worse on a consistent basis personally it just feels like it starts to kill that joy we all felt as kids permenently. I hope this will heed a fair warning to anyone reading this.

I initially gave this game a miss due to it being yet another trio only shooter where trying to play alone just puts you at a disadvantage, but after playing it just to receive a skin in arc raiders I found myself pulled in by the unique game mode and wanting to continue playing.

There's definitely a disadvantage to playing solo with 2 random teammates, but its countered somewhat by there being absolutely no matchmaking whatsoever. You can end up with the highest ranked thousands of hours played random teammates that wipe the floor with everyone singlehandedly while you just watch or end up on a team that has a collective 10 matches played and be one getting wiped.

It makes for a game where winning or losing or even your own personal performance rarely matters at all. It's all just about the moment to moment gameplay and making cool plays in a game mode that can only be found here. So if you're only interested in an FPS if its this perfectly balanced skill based experience where your own personal skill is the make or break for winning or losing then you will be frustrated to no end and hate this game.

However if you can put aside the fact that you'll be put into deeply unfair situations where you have no hope of winning and just enjoy making the most of those bad situations as they arise with no concern for the outcome then theres definitely something special here that can't be found in any other game. The thing that separates this game from others with a similar issue like hero shooters or mobas is that the elimination style of the game means that if you end up being the team getting screwed that it'll be over quickly.

In a moba game for example you're having to bet the next hour of your life on the performance of the random people you get matched with under punishment of getting banned if you leave making you wish for the sweet release of death in a really bad game, but here a really bad game just means you're eliminated first and its over after only 10 minutes. It makes it so you're only having to invest time into matches that are promising rather than being stuck in the bad ones for so long that you're afraid to roll the dice again.

So yeah its definitely a love it or hate it kind of game just based on your tolerance for BS, It's free so there's no real reason why you should've give it a go to see which end you're on, but just know that the onboarding process is rough and you'll be thrown into the deep end almost immediately. They added bot matches shortly before I started playing which can help you understand the basics, but they don't provide enough of a challenge to really prepare you for what actual players are like, so you'll still end up in a trial by fire if you do give it a go.
